title: Photographing the Great Migration
excerpt: Dust, movement and drama: photographing the Great Migration has its own challenges. Practical tips for your camera and your timing.
body:
The migration offers incredible photo opportunities, but it can be overwhelming: thousands of animals, dust and fast action.

## Gear

- A zoom lens of around 100–400 mm is very versatile.
- A wider lens (24–70 mm) for herds in the landscape.
- A beanbag to rest the camera on the vehicle.
- Extra batteries and memory cards.
- A cloth or cover against dust.

See [camera gear for a Tanzania safari](/blog/safari-photography-gear/).

## Settings

- Fast shutter speed (1/1000 s or faster) for action.
- Continuous autofocus and burst mode.
- Try slower shutter speeds with panning for movement.

## Composition

- Show the scale: a wide shot of the herd.
- Look for details: a single wildebeest jumping, splashing water, eyes.
- Use the dust and backlight at sunrise and sunset.

## River crossings

Be ready long before the crossing. Choose your position with your guide and keep the motor running quietly off.

## Respect

Never ask your guide to break rules for a photo. See [safari etiquette](/blog/safari-rules-and-etiquette/).

## Enjoy too

Put the camera down sometimes and just watch. [Plan your photography safari](/travel-proposal/).
